{'text': 'Apple today updated the Mac mini and Mac Studio, adding Wi-Fi 7 support to both product lines for the first time. Below is the complete list of Apple devices that support full Wi-Fi 7 functionality.', 'source': '0'}

{'text': 'Operation in the 6 GHz band is not available in all regions.', 'source': '1'}

{'text': 'Apple today published a support document detailing which of its products fully support Wi-Fi 7.', 'source': '2'}

{'text': 'This list differs from Apple\'s broader list of devices "capable of connecting to Wi-Fi 7 networks," as Wi-Fi 7 is backwards compatible.', 'source': '3'}

{'text': "That means even devices that only support Wi-Fi 6E can connect to a compatible Wi-Fi 7 network and use the 6 GHz band where applicable, even though they don't support the full set of Wi-Fi 7 features.", 'source': '4'}

{'text': 'Wi-Fi 7 features include 320 MHz channels, 4096-QAM, and Multi-Link Operation (MLO), which can deliver higher throughput, better efficiency, and lower latency; you can learn more about that here.', 'source': '5'}

{'text': 'With that said, here is the list of devices that Apple officially says fully support the complete set of Wi-Fi 7 features as of August 2026:', 'source': '6'}

  • {'text': 'MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or M5 Max chip or later', 'source': '7'}
  • {'text': 'MacBook Air with M5 chip or later', 'source': '8'}
  • {'text': 'Mac mini with M5 Pro chip or later', 'source': '9'}
  • {'text': 'Mac Studio with M5 Max chip or later', 'source': '10'}
  • {'text': 'iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, or later (excluding iPhone 16e, iPhone 17e)', 'source': '11'}
  • {'text': 'iPhone Air', 'source': '12'}
  • {'text': 'iPad Pro with M5 chip or later', 'source': '13'}
  • {'text': 'iPad Air with M4 chip or later', 'source': '14'}

{'text': 'Apple notes that "Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 functionality operating in the 6 GHz band is only available in regions where the spectrum allows unlicensed Wi-Fi use," adding that "if your region has not approved operation in this manner, your device will only use the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands to connect to Wi-Fi."', 'source': '15'}

{'text': 'To learn more about Wi-Fi 7 availability on Apple devices, visit this link.', 'source': '16'}
